details: On August 2nd, 2026, President Trump announced a pause on planned US military strikes against Iran, citing requests from Tehran and other Middle Eastern nations, and hinted at a potential deal. The proposed agreement would aim to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and address Iran's nuclear program. This de-escalation led to a notable rebound in Bitcoin's price, which had previously fallen to an 18-day low amid rising tensions. However, Iranian media denied requesting the halt and stated the Strait of Hormuz remains closed while hostile actions continue.
title: Trump Halts Iran Strikes, Hints at Deal; Bitcoin Rebounds

details: The United States implemented new tariffs on August 1st, 2026, imposing a 25% duty on Canadian and Mexican goods and 10% on Chinese goods. In response, Canada and China immediately announced retaliatory tariffs, affecting significant volumes of annual imports. This development signals an escalation of global trade tensions with potential broader economic consequences.
title: US Imposes New Tariffs on China, Canada, Mexico; Retaliation Begins

details: A Reuters investigation, reported on August 2nd, 2026, revealed that at least $676 million in cryptocurrency flowed from Shelbit, an unlicensed Dubai-based exchange identified as part of an Iranian sanctions evasion network, to Binance. A substantial portion of these transactions occurred after Dubai regulators took action against Shelbit in January 2025. This highlights ongoing challenges in enforcing sanctions within the crypto space.
title: $676 Million in Iran-Linked Crypto Moved to Binance, Reuters Reports

details: On August 2nd, 2026, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) announced its commitment to timely adjustments of monetary policy tools and maintaining ample liquidity to bolster the nation's economy. This pledge follows a call from the Politburo to accelerate fiscal spending, as China's second-quarter economic growth marked its slowest pace in over three years.
title: China's Central Bank Pledges Loose Monetary Policy Amid Economic Challenges

details: Trump Media and Technology Group launched a subscription-based data service on August 1st, 2026, offering financial firms and other paying subscribers real-time, early access to Truth Social posts, including those from President Trump's influential account. This service, which can cost up to $100,000 per month, has sparked ethical concerns regarding potential market manipulation and insider trading, given the President's frequent use of the platform for policy announcements.
title: Trump Media Sells Early Access to Market-Moving Truth Social Posts
